title: The Friend Of My Friend
text:
The Friend Of My Friend

Louis-Vincent Gave

Gavekal Research | 31 Aug 2026

In mid-September, Chinese president Xi Jinping is expected to visit India for the first time in seven years with a 400-person-strong delegation. This visit seems important as it seems to mark a thaw in the Indian-Chinese relationship; a relationship that has definitely been somewhat frosty in recent years. In fact, we have argued in the past (see Avoiding the Punch) that when it comes to the “great powers” of Eurasia, the India-China relationship stands out like a bit of a sore thumb in that China is now very close friends with Russia, and India, since independence in 1947, has always maintained a very friendly relationship with Moscow. But meanwhile, when it comes to the India-China relationship, it simply has not been true that “the friend of my friend is my friend.”The fact that Russia’s two most important friends do not get along is a bummer for Russia. First, of course, because Russia today does not have so many friends that Russia can afford for its few friends to not get along. But secondly, and much more importantly, because for 150 years, Russia’s business model was to extract commodities and sell these to Western Europe. This business model is now clearly compromised. And so the fact that Russia can no longer sell her commodities to Europe means that Russia has had to look for new markets. And when it comes to commodity demand ex-Western-World, two countries stand out: China and India.
